title: Falcon Patrol
build: Remember crack, 'Falcon Patrol +5 and Highscoresaver 100%', highscore-saver only (no trainers)

records.c: 6510 on-chip port data-direction register (not RAM; the snapshot's RAM image here holds unrelated bytes). This game plays no banking tricks: facts.md records $01 = $37 for the whole run, so BASIC ROM, I/O and KERNAL are all banked in.
6510 on-chip port. Stays $37 throughout, so the VIC bank-0 window at $1000-$1FFF hides the RAM the crack keeps its menu text and documents screen in (see crack_front_end at $1900).
Not a variable. The cold start at $4100 clears zero page with LDX #$70 / STA $02,X / DEX / BNE, so it writes $03-$72 and never touches $02 itself. No other code reads or writes it.

Low byte of a 16-bit screen-RAM pointer ($05/$06). build_screen_ptr at $5800 loads it with $0400 + 40*Y + X (Y in .Y, X in .X) and the matching colour-RAM address into $07/$08; the AAM and bomb drawing at $5840/$58A0/$5960/$59C0 then stores through ($05),Y. The high-score name entry at $4C51-$4CBD reuses the same pair for its own screen pointer.
High byte of the screen pointer built by $5800 (starts at $04 and is INCed once per 256 bytes of row offset).

Low byte of the colour-RAM pointer ($07/$08) that $5800 builds alongside ptr_screen, so a glyph and its colour are written from one row/column pair. $50D0 reuses $07/$08 as a *screen* pointer ($05E0, landscape row 12) for the character scroll, with $09/$0A as the matching colour pointer - the pair is scratch, not dedicated.
High byte of the colour pointer built by $5800 (starts $D8); $50D8 loads $05 here instead when the landscape scroller borrows the pair.
Low byte of the colour-RAM pointer the landscape scroller uses ($09/$0A, set to $D9E0 at $50DA = colour RAM for screen row 12). $50F7-$5100 shifts screen and colour together one character per call.
High byte of the landscape scroller's colour pointer, $D9 at $50DA, INCed at $50CD when the row pointer crosses a page.
Countdown of landscape rows still to shift. $50E0 loads 8 (screen rows 12-19, the landscape band); DECed at $510C (scroll left) and $513A (scroll right), and the routine stops when it reaches zero.
Joystick/keyboard byte after the game has forged it. Not the raw port: altitude limits, take-off and touchdown all rewrite it, and everything downstream believes it.

World scroll position: the column of the terrain/base map at $3800 that is currently at the left of the view. INCed at $50F3 when the landscape scrolls left and DECed at $5123 when it scrolls right. Used as the map index by the landing test ($55B1 reads $3800+$0D+$12 and +$14 and wants glyph $16, an intact base), by the radar at $52F0 ($11 = $0D-$6C), by the wave spawner at $450C and by the base-damage scan at $5F68.

Low byte of a pointer into the terrain map ($0E/$0F, high byte $38 set at $50E4). $50B0 reads the next map glyph through ($0E),Y when the landscape scroller needs a new column; $50BD INCs $0F. Cleared to $00 at $50E8.
High byte of the terrain-map pointer, $38 at $50E4.

General one-byte scratch. Most often the saved X register: $584A, $58AB, $5968 and $59C8 park X here while they call build_screen_ptr ($5800), which needs X for the column, and reload it at $5858/$58C6/$5976. Also holds the wave's spawn column at $4511 and the chosen enemy's slot index at $5C29.

Map column at the left edge of the radar window: $52F2 computes $0D - $6C. $5359 subtracts it from a blip's map column to get the blip's position inside the radar box; $5E1F reaches it as $11,X when the score carry runs.

Score as five decimal digits, most significant first ($12 ten-thousands .. $16 units). $5E10 adds $AA to $16 and carries upward through $11,X; $51C2 copies all five to screen $0770 (row 22, column 0) in colour 1. The 3000-point bonus life at $55E3 tests $13 >= 3. Cleared with the rest of $17-$64 at $5655 when a life starts.

Thousands digit of the score (element 1 of score_digits at $12). Read on its own at $55E3, where a value of 3 or more - a score of 3000 - awards the one bonus life, and at $4A84, part of the sound code.
Hundreds digit of the score (element 2 of score_digits at $12). Read on its own only at $4A8E/$4A98, in the sound code.

Units digit of the score (element 4, the last, of score_digits at $12). $5E13 adds wave_score_value ($AA) straight into it and then carries upward; $5657 clears $17-$64 starting just above it when a life begins.

GAS gauge, hundreds digit. The refuel routine at $5420 stops topping up once this reaches 9, so a full tank is 900-something. $5576 ORs $17/$18/$19 together: all zero sets flight_flags bit 7 (dry), and $17 alone being zero sets bit 6 (under 100 left - the low-fuel warning). $4EB0 uses it as the length of the GAS bar.
GAS gauge, tens digit. INCed at $5439 when the units digit wraps during refuelling, DECed at $5564 when the units digit underflows during consumption.

GAS gauge, units digit; the digit actually burned. $555E DECs it - that instruction is the byte the crack's 'Unlimited GAS ??' trainer overwrites with $A5 (LDA) from $19A6. Burn rate: one unit every other tick at full horizontal deflection (vel_x = $03 or $FD), otherwise one every eighth tick, see $5546-$555A.
Air-to-air missile count, hundreds digit. The rearm loop at $544C only adds missiles while this is zero, which is what caps the load at 100 - the figure the instruction screen at $1D90 quotes.
AAM count, tens digit. INCed at $545A on units wrap, DECed at $57E1 on units underflow.

AAM count, units digit. $57DB DECs it each time a missile is launched - that instruction is the byte the crack's "Unlimited AAM's ??" trainer overwrites with $A5 (LDA) from $19DC. $57A2 refuses to launch when all three digits are zero.

Lives remaining. Set to 3 at $4142 at the start of a game, DECed at $417C when a life ends (the byte the crack's Unlimited LIVES trainer overwrites with $A5 from $19A6), INCed at $55ED for the one 3000-point bonus life, preserved across the $5655 clear by $5651/$565C, and copied to screen $0777 by $51EE. Previously named life_phase; it is a plain counter.

Low byte of a pointer into the character generator where a radar blip is plotted ($1E/$1F, high byte always $36). $5346 selects $36F8 for blip rows 8 and up and $534E selects $3680 for rows below that; $537E/$5382 OR the blip bit into ($1E),Y. This is how the radar is drawn without touching screen RAM.
High byte of the radar blip pointer, always $36 ($5352/$5354).
In: the radar row of the blip to plot (0-15; $5302 passes $0B for a ground base, $531C passes the enemy's row from $47,X). $5371-$537A then overwrites it with the two-bit pixel mask for that column.

In: the map column of the blip to plot ($5302 passes the map index of a base, $5320 the enemy's map column from $4B,X). $5356-$536B turns it into the byte offset inside the radar glyph row, relative to radar_origin ($11).

Flight/state bit set, and the single most consulted byte in the game. bit 0: set at $53BC at the end of the start-of-life drop-in; meaning beyond that not established. bit 1: parked on a refuelling base - $559A sets it only on a pass where sprite 0 Y is exactly $84, vel_x is 0 and the two map cells at $3800+world_x+$12/+$14 are both the base glyph $16, and it then refuels twice; the input gate at $5731 forces $0C to $FE (up only) while it is set, which is the vertical take-off. bit 3: the player has been destroyed - $4400 sets it (preserving bit 4) for every hit the VIC reports, $5774 sets it when the tank has run dry and the aircraft reaches the ground, $4800 plays the crash sound on it, the input gate forces a dive, $41C7/$41D0 end the life on it. bit 4: survives the rewrite at $4404 and $5778; meaning not established. bit 6: fuel below 100, set at $558E. bit 7: fuel exhausted, set at $5582 and cleared by the refuel routine at $5468. NOTE: bit 3 is death, not landing - see $4400.
Written at $5EBE and $5EDA, read at $5EA6. No other access anywhere in the tracked code. Purpose not established.

State byte for the crash / ground-impact sound run by $4800 while flight_flags bit 3 (player destroyed) is set. $4806 calls $4990 to start it when this is zero; $4871 sets it to $90 at the moment of impact, which also gates the noise burst into $D404/$D40B/$D412 and puts the first explosion frame ($88) in the sprite 0 pointer. $567D clears it when a new life starts.
State byte for the sound $4880 plays while flight_flags bit 1 (parked on a base) is set: $4886 tests its sign, $489D and $4A26 write it. Written/read only inside $4880-$48BC and $4A10-$4A2E.
Step counter for the same $4880 sound: $488A/$48A1 read it, $4891/$48AC INC it, $4899/$48B4/$4A01 reload it.

State byte for the low-fuel / dry-tank warning sound at $4900, which runs while flight_flags bits 6-7 are set. $4906 clears it on entry to the warning; $494D starts the idle engine sound at $49F0 when it is zero.
Phase flag of the warning sound at $4900: zero means the rising sweep, non-zero the fall. $4931 sets it and gates the voice-2 gate/frequency at $D40B/$D408.

Working frequency high byte for the warning sound's voice 2: stepped by 2 at $4917 up to $58, then reset, and written straight to $D408 at $491C. $4957-$4963 takes bit 2 of it to flash the GAS bar colour ($2E) in time with the beep.
Horizontal velocity, stepped one unit per 8 passes of tick_counter, clamped to $FD..$03 (-3..+3).
Vertical velocity. Zeroed on touchdown and on ground contact.

Free-running counter INCed once per pass at $5F00, used only to divide the landscape scroll rate: at |vel_x| = 2 the world moves on every other value ($5F16 masks 1), at |vel_x| = 1 on every fourth ($5F1E masks 3), and at |vel_x| = 3 on every pass.
Free-running counter; its low bits pick which part of the flight update runs this pass.

Colour index the GAS bar is repainted in by $4EA0 ($DB8F onwards, screen row 22 columns 31-39). $4963 alternates it between 1 and 2 in step with the low-fuel warning sound, so the bar flashes; $5676 forces 2 at the start of a life. Note the bytes at $2E,X reached by the AAM routines are $31/$34/$37/$3A, not this variable.

One-byte scratch with no single owner: $425E saves a sprite index in it inside the collision handler, $4CD8/$4DD0 use it in the name-entry code, $5D25/$5D3E in the bomb drawing. The $2F,X accesses from $57A8, $5842, $5878 and $58A2 reach $32/$35/$38/$3B - the AAM records, not this byte.

Four air-to-air missiles in flight, three bytes each, at $30, $33, $36 and $39. +0 = screen column (0-$27), +1 = screen row, +2 = direction and occupancy ($00 free, $01 travelling right, $FF travelling left). $57A6-$57CC fills a free slot on a fire press - column $12 or $15, row = ($D001-$28)/8, direction opposite the sign of vel_x - and then DECs the AAM count. $5870 steps each one and frees it once the column leaves 0-$27; $5840 erases the old cell with a space and $58A0 redraws it as glyph $12 (right) or $13 (left) with the colour from the $4000 table. The missiles are character graphics, not sprites.

Not a variable of its own: it is the base the enemy-bomb row array is addressed from, $3B,X with X = 1..4 reaching bomb_rows at $3C-$3F ($5962, $59A2, $5B6C). $412D also DECs $3B,X for X = 8..1 at the cold start, which is what puts $FF in all eight bytes $3C-$43.

Screen rows of the up to four enemy bombs in flight, one byte per bomb at $3C-$3F; $FF means the slot is free. $412D (cold start) and $5662 (new life) fill $3C-$43 with $FF. $5B6C writes the row when an enemy releases a bomb, and $5B50-$5B5E refuses to release one into a row a bomb already occupies.

Screen row of enemy bomb 2 (element 1 of bomb_rows at $3C), $FF when the slot is free. $5B50-$5B5E compares a proposed new bomb's row against $3C, $3D, $3E and $3F in turn and refuses to drop one into a row that is already taken.

Screen row of enemy bomb 3 (element 2 of bomb_rows at $3C), $FF when the slot is free. $5B50-$5B5E compares a proposed new bomb's row against $3C, $3D, $3E and $3F in turn and refuses to drop one into a row that is already taken.

Screen row of enemy bomb 4 (element 3 of bomb_rows at $3C), $FF when the slot is free. $5B50-$5B5E compares a proposed new bomb's row against $3C, $3D, $3E and $3F in turn and refuses to drop one into a row that is already taken.

Screen columns of the same four enemy bombs, at $40-$43, $FF when free. $5B68 sets it from the enemy's on-screen column; $5988-$599E walks the bomb across (one column per pass, direction from $60) and frees both halves of the record when the column leaves 0-$27. $5960 erases and $59C0 redraws the bomb glyph.

Scratch used by the enemy-bomb and base-bombing code: $5B22 holds the enemy's on-screen column, $5C15/$5C27 the highest radar row found among live enemies, $5C53 a counter that seeds the ground-explosion record. Also reached as $44,X by nothing.
Scratch alongside $44: $5B46 holds the enemy's radar row plus one, which becomes the bomb's screen row; $5C47 holds a copy of the chosen enemy's map column.
Scratch alongside $44/$45; $5C4B copies the chosen enemy's third parameter ($4F,X) here before $5C5F files it into the ground-object record.

Base of the four-entry enemy array reached as $47,X with X = 1..4, i.e. the bytes $48-$4B: the aircraft's radar row / height band. Read by the radar plotter at $531C, by the bomb-release test at $5B44 and by the base-bombing chooser at $5C21/$5C41. The byte at $47 itself is index 0 and is used separately as a scratch by $4263, $429D, $45F0 and $5C61.

Base of the enemy array reached as $4B,X (X = 1..4, bytes $4C-$4F): the aircraft's position in world/map columns. $5B1D subtracts world_x from it to get the on-screen column, $5320 passes it to the radar plotter, $5C45 copies it into a bomb record.
World/map column of enemy aircraft 1 (element 1 of enemy_map_x at $4B, reached as $4B,X with X=1). $5EE4 reads it directly.
Base of the enemy array reached as $4F,X (X = 1..4, bytes $50-$53). Copied into the ground-bomb record at $5C49. Which quantity it holds is not established.
Base of the enemy array reached as $53,X (X = 1..4, bytes $54-$57). Copied into the ground-bomb record at $5C4D. Which quantity it holds is not established.

Base of the enemy array reached as $57,X (X = 1..4, bytes $58-$5B): the aircraft's life state, and the value that picks its sprite. $4342 reads it: $00 = slot empty, $01-$CF = flying (shape chosen from blocks $94-$98, mirrored to $99-$9D when $60 is negative), $D0-$DF = shape forced to block $95, $E0 and up = destroyed, drawn as a random one of the debris blocks $88-$8B in white multicolour. $5B19 and $5C1D refuse to let a destroyed aircraft bomb anything.
Life state of enemy aircraft 1 (element 1 of enemy_state at $57, reached as $57,X with X=1). Read directly at $5EAC and $5EC8. See enemy_state for the value ranges.

Base of the enemy array reached as $5B,X (X = 1..4, bytes $5C-$5F). $4372 tests it for zero and then for sign to choose which way the aircraft's attitude frame steps, so it behaves as a per-aircraft manoeuvre direction. DECed at $4655, written from seven sites in $456D-$4683. Not fully established.

Which way the current wave of enemies is coming from. $4520-$4528 sets it to $01 or $FF from a random bit of SID oscillator 3 ($D41B). Everything that has to mirror left/right reads its sign: the enemy sprite frame ($4392 adds 5 to the pointer for the mirrored set), the bomb's drift direction ($598C), the falling-bomb motion ($5C7E) and the base scan ($5F2B).

Bit set of what is currently in play. Bit 0 = a wave of enemy aircraft is up (set at $452C by the wave spawner, tested at $5B00/$5C00/$58D3). Bit 1 = a ground bomb is falling (set at $5C69, cleared at $5E3E once both slots at $A8/$A9 are empty). Bit 2 = an air-dropped bomb record is live (set at $5B70, cleared at $59B8 when the last one has left the screen). $4500 only starts a new wave when bits 0-2 are all clear.

Loaded with $0A at $4125 (cold start) and $5672 (new life); also written at $4AA8 and $4AB5, and read at $4550 and $4AB3. Behaves like a countdown or a phase index shared with the code just below the raster handler, but its meaning is not established.

Cleared at $4532 when a wave is spawned, INCed at $454C and compared at $454E, written again at $4556. Looks like a per-wave counter (how many aircraft have been released), but that is not established.
Map column the current wave enters at. $450C-$451B computes world_x - $A0 plus a random 0-$3F from SID oscillator 3. Read once, at $455F.
Cleared at $4534 when a wave is spawned, INCed at $4558, read at $4546, $455A, $45FE and $5EC2. Purpose not established.
Loaded with $04 at $4129 (cold start), also written at $4A82 and $4AA0; read at $4548, $4600, $4AA2 and $4AAA. Purpose not established.

Bonus-life state. $55DF only awards the 3000-point extra life while this is zero, and $55EB then sets it to $30, so the bonus can only ever be given once per game; $41EE clears it when the title screen is entered. While it is non-zero $4FA0-$4FBC plays the bonus fanfare on SID voice 2 and INCs it, so it runs $30..$FF and wraps back to zero; $494D's idle engine sound and $4FC0's warning sound are suppressed meanwhile.

One frame's worth of the VIC's sprite-to-sprite collision register. $4204 reads $D01E into it once per pass, because reading that register clears it, and everything downstream works off this copy. Bit 0 is the player: $420F calls player_hit ($4400). Bits 5 and 6 are the two enemy bombs on sprites 5 and 6: $4218-$4227 cancels the matching bomb record by zeroing $A8/$A9. Bits 1-4 are the enemy aircraft: $4231-$423F calls $4303 for each one that collided.

One frame's worth of the VIC's sprite-to-background collision register, read once at $4241 from $D01F for the same reason. Bit 0 is the player hitting the landscape, which calls player_hit at $424C. Bits 1-4 are the enemy aircraft hitting a background character - and since the player's air-to-air missiles are character graphics (the records at $30-$3B, drawn as glyphs $12/$13), this is the only path by which a missile can register a hit on an aircraft. That the register latches and is cleared by the single read is a plausible explanation for the missed hits the wiki reports, but it has not been tested.

$90-$FF is the KERNAL's own zero page. The crack's save routine zeroes all of it at $290F-$2916 before calling SETLFS/SETNAM/SAVE, so the KERNAL starts from a clean state; the game itself uses $96-$B2 of this area for its own variables while it runs, and they are destroyed by that clear.

Low byte of a pointer ($96/$97) into the aircraft attitude bank at $2B00-$2D7F. $5A38 loads $2CC0 (level, nose right) when vel_x reaches +3 and $5A4C loads $2B80 (level, nose left) when it reaches -3; $5A73/$5A82 then steps it by $40 - one sprite block - per unit of $99. $5AC4 copies the 64 bytes it points at into sprite block $86 ($2180) and $5AD0 into block $80 ($2000).
High byte of the attitude-bank pointer, $2B or $2C, so the pointer always lands inside $2B00-$2D7F.

Non-zero once the aircraft has reached full deflection and the attitude bank is driving sprite block $80/$86. Set at $5A36/$5A4A, cleared at $5A68 when $99 has returned to zero, and cleared with $98-$B0 at $566B when a life starts. $560C makes the yaw animation at $5600 stand down while it is set.

Signed attitude index, -2..+2, added to ptr_attitude_frame as a count of $40-byte sprite blocks. $5A94-$5AB5 drives it from vertical velocity: vel_y zero walks it back to 0 (level), climbing walks it to +2, diving to -2. Cleared at $566B when a life starts.

Delay constant for the note the title tune is currently sounding. $4BB3 and $4BE4 use it as the inner count of the two timing loops in the player at $4B5D, and $4BF6 reloads it from the duration table at $2AE0 for the next note. $4C3A sets $BF when the SID is silenced.

Index of the current note of the title tune, 0..$1C. $4B6B loads X from it, $4BF5 steps it, $4BFB ends the tune at $1D. It selects one entry from each of the six frequency tables at $2A00-$2ABF and from the duration table at $2AE0. The crack zeroes it at $1A25 before handing over.

Base of a two-entry array reached as $9F,X with X = 1..2, i.e. the bytes $A0/$A1: the falling ground bomb's row. $5C57 seeds it, $5CCC steps it, and $5CD0 ends the bomb when it reaches $13 (the ground).
Base of the two-entry array reached as $A1,X (bytes $A2/$A3): the falling bomb's column. $5C5B seeds it from the enemy's map column; $5C8C/$5CA0 step it as the bomb drifts.

Base of the two-entry array reached as $A3,X (bytes $A4/$A5): a sub-column accumulator - $5CBE adds to it and $5CC8 carries into bomb_ground_col when it passes 8. The collision handler also reaches $A8/$A9 through this base at $4221 (X = 5, 6) to cancel a bomb whose sprite has hit something.
Base of the two-entry array reached as $A5,X (bytes $A6/$A7): a sub-row accumulator, stepped by 2 at $5C82/$5C92 and carried into the row counter at $5C88/$5C9C.

Base of the two-entry array reached as $A7,X (bytes $A8/$A9): non-zero while that bomb slot is in use. $5C34 looks for a free slot, $5CD4-$5CDE clears the whole record when the bomb lands, $4221 clears it when sprite 5 or 6 registers a collision, and $5E36/$5E3A clear active_flags bit 1 once both are empty. Sprites 5 and 6 carry these bombs - $410C points both at sprite block $9E.

Occupancy byte of ground-bomb slot 1 (element 1 of bomb_ground_active at $A7). Non-zero while that bomb is falling; $5E36 tests it, $4221 clears it when $D01E reports a collision on sprite 5, $5CDE clears it when the bomb lands.
Occupancy byte of ground-bomb slot 2 (element 2 of bomb_ground_active at $A7). $5E3A tests it; together with $A8 it decides when active_flags bit 1 is cleared at $5E3E.

Points for the next enemy shot down in this wave. $4538 loads $19 (25) when a wave spawns and $5E2C doubles it after every score, giving 25, 50, 100, 200 - the progression the wiki documents. $5E10 adds it to the score digits at $12-$16.

Working value for the SID filter cutoff high byte ($D416) during the crash sound. $482F ramps it up by 2 to a ceiling of $6D while the wreck falls, $4850 and $48E0 ramp it back down, and $4860 fires the impact noise burst once it drops below $40.
Working frequency high byte for SID voice 1 during the crash sound: INCed at $4811 and clamped to $E0, then written to $D401. Reset by $481B/$49A5/$49D3/$4A3A when a sound starts.
Working frequency high byte for SID voice 3 during the crash sound: INCed at $4820, clamped to $E0, written to $D40F. The pair $AD/$AE is what makes the falling-aircraft whine.

DECed at $42D1, written at $42D9 and $5E8F, read at $42D3 and $5E7F. Both users sit in the scoring / enemy-destruction path, so it behaves like a short countdown there, but its meaning is not established.
Which of the three raster bands the interrupt is about to set up: $FF, $00 or $01.

Countdown that decides how long the title screen waits before dropping back into the demo/attract path. $46E8 loads $E8, $5409 INCs it, and $416C tests it at the start of a life. Not fully established.
Phase counter of the title screen. $46E4 clears it, $4C0E INCs it when the tune is cut short by fire, $4EEF INCs it elsewhere, and $4EE0 and $53E3 read it.

Low byte of the start address the crack's high-score save passes to the KERNAL SAVE at $2935: $2929/$292D set $FB/$FC to $2800, the base of the saved high-score table. Part of the Remember crack, not the game.
High byte of the high-score save's start address, $28 ($292D/$292F).
$0200-$0290, the KERNAL/BASIC input buffer. Neither Steve Lee's code nor the crack writes it while the game runs; it still holds whatever the loader left. Not part of the game.

$0291, the KERNAL's shift-mode flag. The crack writes $80 here at $1910, which disables the Shift+Commodore character-set switch so the player cannot flip the documents screen into the graphics set. The rest of $0292-$0313 is untouched KERNAL workspace.

Low byte of the KERNAL's IRQ vector. $4B20 points it at the game's raster handler; $28A3 puts $31 back and $2909 reloads the whole vector table $0314-$0333 from the KERNAL's copy at $FD30 before the high-score save calls back into the KERNAL.

High byte of the KERNAL's IRQ vector; $28A8 restores $EA. The bytes above it, $0316-$03FF, are ordinary KERNAL workspace (BRK and NMI vectors, tape and RS-232 areas) that neither the game nor the crack uses.
$03FF, the last byte of the system work area. Unused by both the game and the crack; the screen begins at $0400.

Start of the title screen. This is LIVE screen RAM, not a stored copy: $46C5-$46C7 writes $2C to $D018, which moves the VIC's screen base to $0800 (character base stays $3000) for as long as the title is up, and $4716-$4718 writes $1C to put it back to $0400 for play (it reads back as $1D because bit 0 of $D018 is unused). 1000 bytes, $0800-$0BE7, with the sprite pointers at $0BF8. $4420 blanks the whole thing with spaces; rows 0-1 columns 12-27 then get the FALCON PATROL logo from $5B80/$5B90, rows 5/7/9/11/13 the five high-score places, row 17 the PRESS FIRE prompt, row 21 the generated alphabet strip and row 24 the credit line from $2F80. NOTE: facts.md calls this 'a stored copy of the title screen at $0843, stamped onto $0400'. It is neither stored nor at $0843: the VIC is simply pointed at it.

Title screen row 0, columns 12-27: the top half of the FALCON PATROL logo, 16 glyphs copied here from $5B80 by $44D1. They are shape glyphs from the game's own character set, not letters of the alphabet at $81-$9A.
Row 1, columns 12-26: bottom half of the FALCON PATROL logo, 16 glyphs copied from $5B90 by $44D7-$44DC. Colour RAM rows 0 and 1 are set to 7 and 5 by $44C0.
Title screen row 1, columns 12-27: the bottom half of the FALCON PATROL logo, 16 glyphs copied here from $5B90 by $44D7. Together with $080C it makes a two-row-tall title in custom glyphs.

Inside title screen row 1, column 27 - nothing starts here. This address carried the label 'title_screen_image' and the claim in facts.md that a 1000-byte copy of the title screen lives here and is stamped onto $0400. It is not a copy and it is not the base: the title screen is live screen RAM at $0800 (see title_screen), selected by $D018 = $2C at $46C5.
Row 2: blank spacer between the logo and the high-score table.
Row 3: blank spacer above high-score rank 1.

The Remember crack's boot menu - not Steve Lee's code. Entered before the game and never returned to; it ends with JMP $4100, the game's cold start. Sequence: clear the screen ($E544), $D018 = $16 so the VIC shows screen $0400 with the ROM character set (the RAM at $1800-$1FFF is invisible to the VIC in bank 0, which is why the crack parks its text there), border and background black, colour RAM all $0F, then copy documents_screen $1C00-$1FFF onto $0400-$07FF and wait at $1948 for $DC01 = $EF - fire on port 1, which is also SPACE, the key the screen at $1FC0 asks for. Then it paints three colour bars, prints crack_banner ($1A80, three rows) and asks 'Highscore or Trainers?' via GETIN ($FFE4): 'H' skips to $1A18, 'T' first pokes $AD over the JSR opcode at $4D73 so the high-score save is disabled, then asks five trainer questions in turn, each printed at screen row 2 from $1AF8, $1B20, $1B48, $1B70 and $1B98 and each answered Y/N; a 'Y' pokes a single byte into the game: $417C -> $A5 (DEC lives becomes LDA, unlimited lives), $555E -> $A5 (unlimited GAS), $57DB -> $A5 (unlimited AAMs), $5F71 -> $4D (the BEQ after CMP #$16 jumps to the already-destroyed path, so bases are indestructible) and $420F/$424C -> $AD (both JSR player_hit become LDA, no collisions). Finally it prints $1BC0, zeroes music_note_index, and waits for 'R' or 'L': 'R' jumps to $2918 to SAVE a fresh high-score file, 'L' does SETLFS 1,8,1 / SETNAM 'F.PATROL HI /REM' / LOAD to $2800 and then JMP $4100. Inputs: keyboard via GETIN and $DC01. Side effects: it writes $D018, $D020, $D021, $D011, $D800-$DBFF, all of screen RAM, and up to seven bytes of the game's own code.

The immediate operand of the LDA #$00 at $294E. Last step of the cascade: copy rank 4 (score $09C2, name $09CD) down into rank 5 ($0A12/$0A1D). Entry point of the $294E cascade; five score digits and twelve name characters per rank, on the live title screen.

Calls $2992 first, then copies rank 1 ($08D2/$08DD) down into rank 2 ($0922/$092D), vacating rank 1. Entry point of the $294E cascade; five score digits and twelve name characters per rank, on the live title screen.
